blocks.text: Daniel set the newspaper beneath a tin of screws, leaving the robbery report uncovered.
Then he cleared a space on the bench for the Army ray.
Its gray casing bore a scrape from the demonstration grounds. The copper rings around the barrel were dull with fingerprints. Neither had anything to do with the ruined collector upstairs.
He wiped the rings with a cloth and checked the switches.
blocks.alt: Dork checks the intact Army ray at his workshop bench beside an empty steel toolbox.

blocks.text: Jaws drifted nearer.
Daniel put an empty steel toolbox on the far end of the bench and closed its lid. He moved a jar of washers out of the way.
Jaws came around to his shoulder to watch.
Daniel selected blue and aimed.
The toolbox dwindled where it stood. Its handle folded down against a lid scarcely wider than his thumb.
Jaws lowered himself to look.
“Don’t bite it.”
“I was looking.”
Daniel picked up the little box between finger and thumb. He turned it once, checking its hinges, then set it back in the cleared space.
Red restored it. The handle struck the lid with a familiar clack.
He opened the box. Empty, exactly as he had left it.
Jaws’s iron teeth spread into a grin.
Daniel laid the ray down with its switches off and turned toward the tank.
The tank stood beneath the high workshop windows, its long gun pointing toward the closed loading doors. Daniel pulled a wooden crate alongside the hull and climbed onto the track.
Jaws rose beside him.
“Bring the oilcan.”
The head turned, spotted it on the bench and sailed over. He caught the can’s loop handle between two teeth and brought it back without spilling a drop.
Daniel took it.
blocks.alt: Jaws floats well above the tank, clearly separated from its turret, while Dork reaches up to accept the oilcan held by its loop handle.

blocks.text: Jaws looked pleased enough to have carried the whole bench.

A folded instruction booklet lay beside the driver’s hatch. Daniel had found it in the tank after the theft. He opened it to the marked page, checked the position of the controls and lowered himself into the driver’s compartment.
Jaws hovered above the opening.
“Stand clear.”
“I don’t stand.”
“Then float clear.”
Jaws backed away, still grinning.
The starter labored. Daniel stopped, checked the booklet again and tried once more.
The engine caught with a roar that filled the workshop.
Jaws darted upward in delight. A loose sheet of paper slid off a crate beside the exhaust.
Daniel kept the tank stationary. He watched the instruments, listened, then shut the engine down. The sudden quiet rang in his ears.
Laura stood in the inner doorway.
“Are you planning to bring the building down?”
Daniel climbed out and retrieved the booklet.
“Not this one.”
Laura watched him descend. Her coat hung open over the flame-patterned black suit. She had tied her brown hair back, but one curl had worked loose beside her mask.
He took a flat steel offcut from beneath the bench and propped it against the brick wall, with clear floor around it.
“Let’s see what you can do with that.”
Laura looked at the metal.
The last time she had tried, her shot had left a shallow scorch. She had hidden the piece before either of them could see it.
Jaws drifted alongside the new target.
“Go on.”
“Move,” she said.
He moved immediately, pleased to be included.
Daniel waited beside the bench.
Laura drew off one glove, straightened its fingers and put it on again.
“A scrap off your floor?” Laura folded her arms. “Find me a real job.”
For a moment he studied her. She kept her eyes on his, although she wanted to look away from the target.
blocks.alt: Laura folds her arms and avoids demonstrating her plasma while Dork indicates a steel target and Jaws encourages her.

blocks.text: Then his gaze went to the newspaper beneath the screw tin.
Jaws looked from one to the other, waiting eagerly for someone to explain it.
Daniel pulled the newspaper free and spread it beside the Army ray.
“The boy couldn’t move a rubbish bin. The girl couldn’t catch a car.”
Laura glanced at the account. Pink Blur’s name caught her eye.
Laura kept her expression blank.
Jaws leaned over the paper.
“Then we go and get them.”
Daniel shook his head.
“First we need money. Fuel. Parts. Equipment that hasn’t been dragged out of a wreck.” Daniel looked around the workshop. “And no more asking Eleanor Blackwell whether I may have it.”
Laura pulled out a stool but did not sit.
“Another jewelry store?”
“That would be a poor use of this.”
He rested one hand on the ray’s casing.
“We’ll take a vault.”
Laura looked up.
“The money in a vault?”
“The vault.”
He moved the toolbox between them. One ordinary steel container, with its hinges and latch intact.
“Bring it here small. Restore it where we can work undisturbed.”
“And open it?” Laura asked.
Daniel glanced toward the offcut still waiting against the wall.
“You wanted something worth burning.”
Jaws gave a delighted clatter of teeth.
Laura’s fingers tightened on the stool’s back. She released them before Daniel looked down.
Daniel went out alone that afternoon.

He left the ray locked in a steel cabinet. The tank remained inside, engine silent. Jaws wanted to come, but a floating head with iron teeth would have made it difficult to stand quietly on a sidewalk.
“Watch the workshop,” Daniel told him.
Jaws accepted the task with immediate importance.
Laura stayed behind too, leaving the steel offcut untouched.

The first bank Daniel passed had its vault deep inside the main building. Taking a door would leave him with a door. Taking the room around it would mean masonry, pipes and floors he could not simply carry away.
He kept walking.
At another branch, scaffolding covered the upper windows. A notice directed customers to the entrance beside the annex while renovation work continued.
Daniel crossed the street.

Beyond the annex’s open delivery doors stood a large steel strongroom on a raised transport frame. Its walls, floor and roof formed a single enclosed unit. He could see daylight beneath the frame and clear space between its sides and the brickwork.
A worker rolled an empty pallet truck out of the doorway. Behind him, a bank guard watched an employee close the strongroom’s heavy door.
Daniel stopped beside a bus-stop sign.
He had seen temporary vaults advertised for banks undergoing construction. This one had been set inside the annex rather than built into it. The surrounding room would stay where it was.
The steel box was the thing he needed to take.
Across the street, the guard turned to a second employee. Daniel lowered his eyes to the bus timetable until the man looked away.
He had no ray with him. He would need to check more than a glimpse through a doorway before bringing it.
But he could see the whole vault.
And he could picture it on his bench, small enough to fit beside the toolbox.
The delivery doors began closing.
blocks.alt: Dork studies a bank under renovation and its freestanding vault from a bus stop across the street.

blocks.text: Daniel watched until the last narrow strip of steel disappeared behind them. Then he took a small notebook from his pocket and wrote the bank’s name.
